method: Every starter of every sheet below was read from two hosts on the read date. nfl.com: the official game book PDF linked from the nfl.com game page ('Download Game Book (PDF)'), page 1 'Lineups' block, read with pypdf text extraction; the game book prints the starters as position, jersey number and initial plus surname. pro-football-reference.com: the box score page's Starters table for that team (#vis_starters or #home_starters, which the site ships inside an HTML comment), read from the rendered page in a browser. A sheet ships only when both hosts list the same eleven men; a sheet where they differ on any starter is held out. Positions are the game book's (pfr prints generic OL labels on some tables). Each blank candidate fact is read from the same two hosts (the game book scoring summary or substitution list and the pfr scoring table). Wikipedia was not used.
nationalityMethod: The first hint says Nationality. Every blank on a Round 950 sheet carries USA because two hosts put his birthplace in a US state: his pro-football-reference.com player page (pfrPlayer, bornPerPfr) and his espn.com athlete record (espnPlayer, bornPerEspn, read 2026-10-03 from ESPN's athlete API; the id came from that Super Bowl's ESPN box score where he has a line, and from ESPN's player search where he does not). Both hosts put all 62 in a US state, which is the fact the hint states. They print the same town for 51 of 62 and the same state for 58; where they differ (cityAgrees false) espn.com mostly prints what reads as a hometown (Garcon: Carmel, NY on pfr, West Palm Beach, FL on espn.com), and both towns are in the US either way, so the hint stands. ESPN prints two men under another first name (espnName: Scotty Miller, Jonathan Stinchcomb), and the file accepts that name as a guess. Four men had no second birthplace read anywhere (espn.com has none on file, nfl.com prints no hometown for them): Jake Ballard, Dan Connolly, Kyle DeVan and Matt Spaeth. They stay on their sheets as starters, which two hosts confirm, and are held out of the blanks (heldBlanks on the sheet).
venueMethod: The line under each sheet reads stadium, city. The game book prints it on page 1 (venueAsPrinted). The second read is the profootballarchives.com box score for the same game ("Location" and "Venue", venueReads), which prints the stadium under its name on the day. The espn.com game summary is a third read for the city only: ESPN names some stadiums by their current name (State Farm Stadium for University of Phoenix Stadium, Hard Rock Stadium for Sun Life Stadium, Caesars Superdome for the Mercedes-Benz Superdome). One disagreement: for Super Bowl LVIII the game book and espn.com print Las Vegas, NV, and profootballarchives.com prints Paradise, NV, the unincorporated town the stadium stands in. The sheet keeps Las Vegas, which two hosts print and which the league uses.

On 2026-10-03 the game book (WR Burress, LT Diehl, LG Seubert, C O'Hara, RG Snee, RT McKenzie, TE Boss, WR Toomer, QB Manning, TE M.Matthews, RB Jacobs) and pfr #vis_starters agree 11/11, but the file dropped this side in an earlier round because its sources then disagreed on the 11th starter. Left out here rather than overturning that call without the third source that disagreed; the lead can add it from this row.

legacyRecheck.note: The 16 sheets written before Round 950 whose notes named fewer than two hosts, reread on 2026-10-03 from the same two hosts as the new sheets. The file keeps its own position labels for these (pfr style in places), so the third column is matched on the surname only. Every one agreed 11/11; nothing on them changed. Added 2026-10-05: the SB XXXV Ravens defense, whose note had leaned on a Wikipedia mirror (reference.org), a video site and a blog repost. It was reread from the league game book and the profootballarchives.com box score; its fourth column is the pfa row (secondHostColumn) because pro-football-reference.com answered with a bot check. Names agree 11/11; the safety labels disagree and the sheet keeps the game book's (disagreements).
